correctness.rationale: The proof derives the centered ellipsoid Holmes--Thompson volume from the polar-volume density, converts the radial integral by t=tanh(s), and substitutes the published exact Hanner volume. The desired two-radius inequality is equivalent to monotonicity of z^(-n) integral_0^z sinh(s)^(n-1) ds, which after s=zu is an integral of positive weights times (sinh(zu)/(zu))^(n-1). Since sinh(x)/x is strictly increasing for x>0, the quotient is strictly increasing for every n>=2.

value.rationale: The source explicitly presents the two-radius inequality as a strengthening of its Hanner-volume conjecture and compares it with Bishop--Gromov theory. Ellipsoids are the canonical smooth affine bodies and appear in the same section as the comparison model for the opposite direction. An all-dimensional strict verification for ellipsoids is therefore a natural structural special case, not an arbitrary parameter slice, and the exact monotone quotient supplies a reusable benchmark.
